liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Peggy-O** (2 reviews): Peggy-O features perfect solos, with Garcia's playing noted as technically proficient and accurate; Garcia's fluid solos and Weir's rhythmic work are praised, marking a peak in their playing style [10][12]

## The recordings

- **gd1978-04-14.sbd.miller.83717.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 170 min; rated 4.63/5 by 30 [1]. Said about its sound: Recording captures the heavy rhythm of Big River with notable power and clarity; Jerry's guitar playing is described as sublime throughout the performance [6][9]
- **gd1978-04-14.148291.sbd.betty.dalton.miller.sirmick.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 170 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [2]
- **gd1978-04-14.147790.shure.sm57.sublette.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 176 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [3]
- **gd1978-04-14.149542.BettyBoard.Anon.Noel.t-flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 168 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [5]

## Around the show

- Keith plays guitar on Dupree's Diamond Blues, as Brent had not joined the band yet [7]
- A college baseball player from ODU heard the show from the team room under the coliseum [15]
- The reviewer found the show while searching for Dancing In The Street, noting sympathetic playing [16]
- Drums features Jerry, Bob, Phil, and road crew, with Mickey playing a synthesizer-like percussion instrument [5]
- This is considered the best Peggy-O of 1978, with another good version at Huntington Civic Center [11]
- The listener agrees that the Peggy-O performance is top shelf quality [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1978-04-14.sbd.miller.83717.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> PCM -> Dat (44.1k) D [1]. Also: Charlie Miller is credited for the recording and transfer of this show; Charlie Miller's transfers and remasters are highlighted as the best available for this date; Charlie Miller is thanked for the recording effort [6][11][16]
- **gd1978-04-14.148291.sbd.betty.dalton.miller.sirmick.flac16**: taped by Betty Cantor;Tim Dalton; transferred by Sirmick and Charlie Miller; source: Source: SBD Master Reel (7" two track @ 7 1/2 ips - recorded by Betty Cantor) > PCM501ES @ 44.055 kHz > DAT (44k) - From the Tim Dalton collection. [2]. Also: A tape flip in Drums was patched using a copy provided by Tim Dalton [2]
- **gd1978-04-14.147790.shure.sm57.sublette.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Kathy Sublette; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Kathy Sublette's Master Audience Cassettes; Shure SM57 mics > Sony-TC158 [3]. Also: This is the first audience source in general circulation for this specific date; An eight-second patch for the Me And My Uncle to Big River transition came from the soundboard [3]
- **gd1978-04-14.149542.BettyBoard.Anon.Noel.t-flac16**: taped by Betty Cantor; transferred by PCM provided by anonymous, while hiding out away from the Bay Area. Edited & Mastered using Adobe Audition by Joe Noel April 12, 2020; source: Source: Betty Cantor’s SBD Reel Master > Beta tape > Beta VCR > PCM [5]
